newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Promet acquires 32.9 pct of Westmont.
newsitem.headline: Promet acquires 32.9 pct of Westmont.

text.p: Malaysia's Promet Industries Bhd said on Friday it was acquiring a 32.9 percent stake in maritime engineering concern Westmont Industries Bhd.
Promet said in a statement on Friday it would spend "close to half a billion ringgit" to acquire the stake.

The stake would consist of 76.68 million shares, and would be satisfied by a cash consideration of 498.44 million ringgit, or 6.50 ringgit per share, said Promet's statement. It would be bought from Westmont Holdings Bhd.
The acquisition would be financed by bank borrowings and internally generated funds, the company said.

Following the proposed acquisition, Westmont's wholly-owned subsidiary Sabah Shipyard Sdn Bhd (Saship) will enter into an agreement with Westmont Holdings' wholly-owned subsidiary Westmont Management Services Sdn Bhd.

In return Westmont Holdings would guarantee Saship an annual pre-tax profit of not less than 120 million ringgit for the financial years ending December 31 1997, 1998 and 1999, Promet's statement said.
The profit guarantee would be secured against a revolving bank guarantee of 50 million ringgit and a corporate guarantee by Westmont Holdings of 70 million.
"The latest acquisition of WIB (Westmont Industries Bhd) will further add to the expertise and network of the Promet Group," said Promet.
Westmont's principle industries include engineering, construction and the servicing and repair of ships, said Promet.

The acquisition would not have a material effect on the earnings per share of the Promet group for the financial year ending December 31, 1996, but would contribute positively to earnings in the future, the company said.
